content:
Attorneys representing a former Cornell University student, who is suing the school over an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house, issued a searing response to the university president’s pledge to review the future of on-campus Greek life following a faculty vote of no-confidence.

“True accountability is not achieved through reactive public relations milestones; it is measured by how an institution treats survivors before the public is watching,” the attorneys’ statement read.

Cornell President Michael I. Kotlikoff in a Monday letter announced a future review of the university’s Greek system in addition to a partnership with New York State Police and the hiring of a new victim advocate in the school’s Sexual Harassment and Assault Response & Education office, among other on-campus safety and prevention efforts.

“I know many in our community have lost confidence in the Cornell administration’s ability to prevent and respond to sexual violence,” Kotlikoff wrote. “I am committed to doing the necessary work to rebuild that confidence: regularly communicating and engaging about the work we have been doing and will do to build a culture of care and responsibility.”

The university’s faculty senate earlier this month passed a resolution of no-confidence in the administration’s ability to handle the ongoing crisis of sexual assault. At least 35% of undergraduate women at Cornell said they experienced an act of nonconsensual sexual contact, a 2025 survey conducted by the university found.

Cornell leadership’s apparent failure to ensure student safety is among the chief complaints in a federal lawsuit filed by the former student, identified as Jane Doe, against the university and others over an alleged gang rape at the Chi Phi fraternity house in 2024.

“For years, Cornell has offered halfhearted measures while rates of campus sexual violence have remained persistently high,” Jane Doe’s attorneys wrote.

It continued: “The University’s decision to review its Greek system, partner with external law enforcement, and expand survivor advocacy comes only after Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit, endured relentless public scrutiny, and helped catalyze a global movement of survivors.”
